Data source overview  
The paper critiques engagement-based recommendation objectives and presents a measurement-theory-grounded latent-variable approach that models an unobservable construct “Value” with a Bayesian network and an anchor-variable identification scheme.  Implemented on Twitter notifications, it shows how to derive and continually update an objective P(Value=1 | Behaviors) that can replace ad-hoc engagement proxies.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]  
The fabric covers every causal path the paper gives from the core risk (engagement–value misalignment) through methodological claims, model components, findings, validation steps, to four actionable interventions.  Nodes were named at the phenomenon/mechanism granularity requested, all edges reference the closest paper sections, and every node participates in the connected graph.  Remaining uncertainty stems from interpreting lifecycle stages for recommender-system work versus the AI-model lifecycle used in the rubric.

Inference strategy justification  
Where the paper implies but does not label an intervention (e.g. scheduled retraining to handle behavioral drift), moderate inference (confidence 2) was applied and marked.  All other edges are directly grounded in explicit statements or demonstrated implementations.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All key concepts the paper relies on—partial correlation of engagement, heterogeneous evidence strengths, measurement theory, latent variable/value construct, Bayesian network structure, anchor variable strategy, identification method, validity evaluation, drift handling—are individually represented so that downstream sources that reuse them will merge correctly.

Key limitations  
1. The paper focuses on recommender systems, so transferability to general foundation-model safety is conceptual rather than empirical.  
2. Some confidence scores are judgement calls because the paper is largely theoretical with one large-scale case study but few controlled experiments.  
3. Lifecycle mapping from recommender deployment to the 6-stage ML lifecycle may need refinement in the global ontology.
